Rashi on Yevamot 48a:10:1.hebrew: עשיה בראש - כלומר, נאמר שם תיקון מצוה בראש, דכתיב וגלחה:
Rashi on Yevamot 48a:10:1.english: Doing with regard to the head - That is to say, the performance of a mitzvah is stated there with regard to the head, as it is written: "and she shall shave [her head]."

Rashi on Yevamot 48a:11:1.english: He had not done his feet - He had not cut the nails of his feet.

Rashi on Yevamot 48a:11:2.english: And he had not done his mustache - He did not shave the hair of his mustache. Thus, [Scripture] calls removal "doing."

Rashi on Yevamot 48a:1:1.hebrew: ומותר בה מיד - אלמא לר' שמעון עבד אין צריך לקבל בשעת טבילת שחרור, ולרבנן דלא הוי תקנתא בהכי, סברי צריך לקבל:
Rashi on Yevamot 48a:1:1.english: And he is permitted to [marry] her immediately - Evidently, according to Rabbi Shimon, a slave does not need to accept [mitzvot] at the time of immersion for emancipation, whereas according to the Rabbis, since there is no remedy through this, they hold [that] he must accept [mitzvot].

Rashi on Yevamot 48a:2:1.hebrew: עבד איש ולא עבד אשה - בתמיה! ואשה שקנתה עבדים ולא מלו, מי לא הוו כשאר עבדים? אלא ע"כ האי "איש" אעובד כוכבים שמכרו קאי, ולמעוטי בן איש. וה"ק: עבד שלקחת מן העובד כוכבים — אתה מל בעל כרחו של עבד, ואי אתה מל בן עובד כוכבים בעלמא, דלאו עבד, בעל כרחו. ומדכתב רחמנא "איש" קרא יתירא למעוטי בן איש, ש"מ "ומלתה אותו" בעל כרחו משמע, דאי מדעתו — היכי ממעט לבן איש? ואי לא כתיב "איש", ה"א האי "עבד" לאו למעוטי בן אתא, אלא היא גופא איצטריך לאשמועינן דמילת עבדים מעכבא בפסח. לשון אחר, ועיקר: "עבד איש" ה"ק: עבד שהוא איש — אע"פ שהוא גדול ובן דעת — ומלתה אותו בעל כרחו, ואי אתה מל בן [שהוא] איש — גר הבא להתגייר, אין לו כח למול בנו גדול בעל כרחו, דגבי בנים כתיב "המול לו כל זכר" ולא כתיב בהו "איש", וגבי עבד כתיב "איש" למעוטי בן:
Rashi on Yevamot 48a:2:1.english: A slave of a man, and not a slave of a woman - [This is asked] in astonishment! If a woman bought slaves and they were not circumcised, would they not be like other slaves? Rather, perforce, this [word] "man" refers to the idolater who sold him, and [comes] to exclude the son of a man. And this is what [the verse] is saying: a slave whom you bought from the idolater — you may circumcise against the slave's will, but you may not circumcise the son of an ordinary idolater, who is not a slave, against his will. And since the Merciful One wrote "man" [as] a superfluous [word in the] verse to exclude the son of a man, learn from this [that] "and you shall circumcise him" implies against his will; for if [it meant] with his consent, how would [it] exclude the son of a man? And if "man" were not written, I would have said [that] this [mention of] "slave" does not come to exclude a son, but rather it itself was needed to teach us that the circumcision of slaves is essential for [eating] the Paschal offering. Another explanation — and [this is] the primary one: "A slave of a man" — this is what [the verse] is saying: a slave who is a man — even though he is an adult and of sound mind — "and you shall circumcise him" against his will, but you may not circumcise a son [who is] a man — [meaning] a convert who comes to convert does not have the authority to circumcise his adult son against his will. For regarding sons it is written, "let every male of his be circumcised," and "man" is not written regarding them; whereas regarding a slave, "man" is written to exclude a son.

Rashi on Yevamot 48a:3:1.hebrew: ורבנן - כשם שאין אתה מל בן איש [בע"כ], דהא לא כתיב בהו איש:
Rashi on Yevamot 48a:3:1.english: And the Rabbis - Just as you do not circumcise a son who is a man [against his will], for "man" is not written regarding them.

Rashi on Yevamot 48a:3:2.hebrew: כך אי אתה מל כו' - ומילתא בעלמא היא ולא הקישא, אלא ה"ק ליה: כי היכי דמודית לן בבן, ה"ה לעבד נמי, דאין מגיירין בן דעת אלא מרצונו:
Rashi on Yevamot 48a:3:2.english: So you may not circumcise, etc. - And this is a general statement and not a [formal] analogy; rather, this is what he is saying to him: Just as you concede to us regarding a son, the same applies to a slave as well, for we do not convert a person of sound mind except with his consent.

Rashi on Yevamot 48a:5:1.english: Say that you heard the Rabbis - who disagree with Rabbi Shimon, [holding] that it is not a remedy.

Rashi on Yevamot 48a:5:2.hebrew: ביפת תואר דלא שייכא במצות אבל עבד - ששהא אצלו כמה ימים וניהג עליו מצות הנוהגות בעבד, מי שמעת להו דצריך לקבל:
Rashi on Yevamot 48a:5:2.english: With regard to a beautiful female [captive], who was not involved in mitzvot; however, [with regard to] a slave - who stayed with him [for] several days and practiced the mitzvot that apply to a slave, did you hear them [say] that he needs to accept [mitzvot]?

Rashi on Yevamot 48a:8:1.hebrew: לענין טבילה תניא - ששניהם שוים בטבילה, שצריכים לטבול כשבאין לכלל ישראל גמור. אבל לענין קבלה לא הושוו, דעבד אין צריך לקבל בשעת טבילת שחרור:
Rashi on Yevamot 48a:8:1.english: With regard to the matter of immersion it is taught - For both of them are equal with respect to immersion, in that they must immerse when they enter into full-fledged Israelite [status]. However, with respect to acceptance [of mitzvot] they were not equated, as a slave does not need to accept [them] at the time of [his] immersion of emancipation.

Rashi on Yevamot 48a:9:1.hebrew: תקוץ - אצפרנים קאי, ואע"ג דלאו ניוול, גזירת הכתוב היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 48a:9:1.english: She shall cut - [This] refers to the nails; and even though [cutting them] is not a disfigurement, it is a scriptural decree.

Tosafot on Yevamot 48a:11:1.hebrew: לא עשה רגליו - פי' בקונטרס צפרני רגליו. ולר"י נראה דהיינו שער בית הערוה, דהכי משמע פרק מצות חליצה (לקמן יבמות קג.) גבי "מן הארכובה ולמעלה חליצתה פסולה", למימרא דלא מיקרי רגל מן הארכובה ולמעלה, תא שמע: "ולא עשה את רגליו", ומשני: לישנא מעליא. מכאן אין ראיה דשרי לגלח שער של בית הערוה, דשמא מדרבנן אסור. אבל בריש פרק ב' נזירים (נזיר נח:) קאמר רב בהדיא: מיקל אדם כל גופו בתער, אפילו שער בית השחי ובית הערוה, כדמשמע התם, דפריך עלה: והתניא "המעביר שער בית השחי ובית הערוה הרי זה לוקה"? ומשני: כי קאמר רב — במספרים. והא "בתער" קאמר! כעין תער. וא"ת: דבתר הכי קאמר: בעי מיניה רב מרבי חייא: מהו לגלח? א"ל: אסור. והא קא גדיל! א"ל: גבול יש לו. משמע דבמספרים בעא מיניה אי שרי, דאי בתער — מאי פריך "והא קא גדיל", והלא יכול לגלח במספרים! ושמא רב לא קבלה מרבי חייא. ור"ת מפרש דבתער בעא מיניה, והא דפריך "והא קא גדיל" ה"פ: והלא אין זה תיקון ואין דומה כלל לתיקוני אשה, שאין זה משום ייפוי אלא משום צער שגדל יותר מדאי, ואפילו בתער אית לן למישרי; ולפי זה צריך לומר שלא היה יודע ברייתא דלעיל שאוסרת. ובה"ג גריס הכי: אמר רב: מיקל אדם כל גופו בתער. והתניא "המעביר" כו'? כי קאמר רב — בשאר אברים. ובשאר אברים מי שרי? והתניא "העברת שער אינו מדברי תורה אלא מדברי סופרים", ומשמע ליה דאיירי ההיא ברייתא אף (בשאר אברים, אע"ג דבבית השחי ובבית הערוה נמי איירי, כדמוכח בתר הכי דכי קאמר רב — במספרים, כי תניא ההיא — בתער; ולפי זה בשאר אברים לא שרי אלא במספרים, ובית השחי ובית הערוה אפי' במספרים אסור, ומדרבנן, דלא תקשי הך דהכא. מיהו בה"ג של אספמיא כתוב: אלא הא בתער והא במספרים, והדר ביה משינויא קמא דשני) כי קאמר רב — בשאר אברים. ולגירסא זו, שאר אברים ודאי אסור לגלח בתער, אבל במספרים שרי אף בית השחי ובית הערוה. ובערוך בערך גינוסטרא גורס כגירסת ספרים שלנו. ובתשובת הגאונים שרי לגלח בית השחי ובית הערוה כי מגלח כל גופו מראשו ועד רגליו, ולא משמע דאיירי במצורע — דפשיטא הוא — אלא במגלח לרפואה, כיון דמגלח כל גופו אין זה ייפוי אלא ניוול. ותדע, דלא משתמיט בשום דוכתא גבי מצורע שיהא עשה דמצורע דוחה לאו ד"לא ילבש גבר", אלא לאו דהקפת הראש וזקן גרידא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 48a:11:1.english: He had not done his feet - Rashi explains [that this refers to] the nails of his feet. But to Rabbi Yitzchak it appears that this refers to the hair of the pubic area, for so it is implied in the chapter [entitled] Mitzvat Chalitzah (below, Yevamot 103a) regarding [the Mishnah]: "[If she removed the shoe] from the knee and above, her chalitzah is invalid" — which is to say that from the knee and above is not called "foot"; [and the Gemara asks:] Come and hear [from the verse]: "And he had not done his feet"! And [the Gemara] answers: [Scripture used] a euphemism. From here there is no proof that it is permitted to shave the hair of the pubic area, for perhaps it is rabbinically prohibited. However, at the beginning of the second chapter of Nezirut [i.e., Nazir] (Nazir 58b), Rav explicitly states: A person may lighten [i.e., shave] his entire body with a razor, even the hair of the armpit and the pubic area — as is implied there, where [the Gemara] challenges this: "Was it not taught [in a Baraita]: One who removes the hair of the armpit and the pubic area incurs lashes?" And [the Gemara] answers: When Rav spoke [of lightening], [he meant] with scissors. [The Gemara asks:] But he said "with a razor"! [And it answers:] Like a razor [i.e., cutting close to the skin as a razor does]. And if you ask: After that, [the Gemara] says: Rav inquired of Rabbi Chiya: "What is [the law regarding] shaving [one's body hair]?" He said to him: "It is prohibited." "But it grows [excessively]!" He said to him: "It has a limit [to its growth]." This implies that he asked him about scissors, whether it is permitted — for if [he asked] about a razor, why did he ask "But it grows," when he could shave with scissors?! [We can answer:] Perhaps Rav did not accept [this ruling] from Rabbi Chiya. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that he asked him about a razor, and [as for] what he asked, "But it grows," this is its meaning: Is this not no [act of] grooming and not at all similar to women's adornments, for this is not for beautification but rather because of distress, as it grows too much, and even with a razor we should permit it? And according to this, one must say that [Rav] was not aware of the Baraita above that prohibits [it]. And in Halakhot Gedolot, the reading is as follows: Rav said: A person may lighten his entire body with a razor. "Was it not taught: One who removes [the hair], etc.?" When Rav spoke, [he was referring] to the other limbs. "And on the other limbs, is it permitted? Was it not taught: Removing hair [from the other limbs] is not by Torah law, but rather by rabbinic law?" — and [the Gemara] understood that that Baraita refers also (to the other limbs, even though it also refers to the armpit and the pubic area, as is proven afterward [when it answers] that when Rav spoke, [he meant] with scissors, [whereas] when that [Baraita] was taught, [it meant] with a razor; and according to this, on the other limbs it is only permitted with scissors, while [for] the armpit and the pubic area, even with scissors it is prohibited, and rabbinically, so that this [Baraita] here should not pose a difficulty. However, in the Halakhot Gedolot of Spain it is written: "Rather, this [Baraita] is with a razor, and that [statement of Rav] is with scissors," and it retracts the first answer that it gave) "When Rav spoke, [he was referring] to the other limbs." And according to this reading, the other limbs are certainly prohibited to shave with a razor, but with scissors even the armpit and the pubic area are permitted. And in the Arukh, under the entry "Ginustra," he reads like the reading of our texts. And in a responsum of the Geonim, it is permitted to shave the armpit and the pubic area when one shaves his entire body from his head to his feet; and it does not seem that [the responsum] is speaking of a metzora — for that is obvious — but rather of one who shaves for medical treatment, [since] because he shaves his entire body, this is not beautification but rather disfigurement. And know [that this is so], for it is never mentioned anywhere regarding a metzora that the positive commandment of a metzora overrides the negative commandment of "A man shall not wear [a woman's garment]," but only the negative commandment of rounding [the corners of] the head and [destroying] the beard:

Tosafot on Yevamot 48a:2:1.hebrew: אלא עבד איש אתה מל בעל כרחו - פי' בקונט' בלשון שני: דעבד איש — אע"ג שהוא גדול ובן דעת — "ומלתה אותו וגו'", בעל כרחו. "ואי אתה מל בן איש": גר הבא להתגייר אין לו כח למול בנו גדול בעל כרחו, דגבי בנים כתיב "המול לו כל זכר", ולא כתיב בהו "כל איש" כמו גבי עבד. ודבר תימה פירש! דקרא ד"המול לו כל זכר" מוקמינן למילת זכריו שמעכבתו מלאכול בפסח, וזה לא שייך אלא בבנים שנולדו בקדושה, אבל מילת בניו שלא נולדו בקדושה אינה מעכבתו מלאכול בפסח. ונראה דלא צריך קרא למידרש מיניה "ואי אתה מל בן איש בעל כרחו", דממילא ידעינן שלא יגיירוהו בעל כרחו; ועוד, דמיפת תואר שמעינן דאין מלין גר בעל כרחו, דהא יפת תואר אין מטבילין אותה בעל כרחה, מדאיצטריך רחמנא להמתין לה שלשים יום, ובקבלה עליה אין צריך להמתין. ולא נקטיה אלא לפרושי מילתיה דרשב"א, דקאמר דמתחלה כופין לשם שפחות ולא לשם גירות. אי נמי, משום דנקט לה במילתיה דרבנן — "כשם שאי אתה מל בן איש" — נקט נמי בדרבי שמעון בן אלעזר, לאשמועינן דאע"פ שאי אתה מל בן איש בעל כרחו, עבד אתה מל בעל כרחו. תימה: דרשב"א קאמר לקמן דאין משהין אותו בא"י מפני הפסד טהרות — עבד שאינו רוצה למול, ומשמע דזקוק למוכרו; ואמאי? ימהלנו בעל כרחו! וכן קשה, דרבי יהושע בן לוי אית ליה בהשולח (גיטין דף לט: ושם): "נתיאשתי מפלוני עבדי — אותו העבד אין לו תקנה אלא בשטר", אלמא לית לי' ההיא דשמואל דבסמוך, וא"כ דריש "עבד איש — אתה מל בעל כרחו"; ולקמן קאמר: "הלוקח עבד מן העובד כוכבים ולא רצה למול — מגלגל עמו עד י"ב חודש", וימול אותו בעל כרחו! ואומר ר"י, דתקנת חכמים היא, שלא יכשיל את רבו באיסור והיתר, כיון דאין מקבל עליו עול מצות; ועוד, דאין טוב לחייבו במצות מאחר דאין חפץ לקיימם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 48a:2:1.english: Rather, "a slave who is a man" — you may circumcise him against his will - Rashi explained in [his] second interpretation that "a slave who is a man" — even though he is an adult and of sound mind — [the verse states,] "and you shall circumcise him, etc.," [meaning] against his will. "But you may not circumcise a son who is a man": a convert who comes to convert does not have the power to circumcise his adult son against his will, for regarding sons it is written, "every male of his shall be circumcised," and it is not written regarding them "every man" as it is regarding a slave. And he explained an astonishing thing! For the verse "every male of his shall be circumcised" we establish [as referring] to the circumcision of his [own] males, which prevents him from eating of the Paschal offering; and this applies only to sons who were born in sanctity, whereas the circumcision of his sons who were not born in sanctity does not prevent him from eating of the Paschal offering. And it appears [to Tosafot] that a verse is not needed from which to expound "but you may not circumcise a son who is a man against his will," for we know on our own that they would not convert him against his will; and furthermore, from [the law of] a captive woman (yefat to'ar) we learn that we do not circumcise a convert against his will, for a captive woman is not immersed against her will, since the Merciful One needed [to command] to wait thirty days for her, whereas if she accepted [conversion] upon herself, there is no need to wait. And [the Gemara] only mentioned it in order to explain the statement of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, who said that initially we coerce [her] for the sake of servitude and not for the sake of conversion. Alternatively, because [the Gemara] mentioned it in the statement of the Rabbis — "just as you may not circumcise a son who is a man" — it also mentioned [it] in [the statement] of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, to teach us that even though you may not circumcise a son who is a man against his will, a slave you may circumcise against his will. This is astonishing: for Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says later on that we do not keep him in the Land of Israel because of the loss of ritually pure foods — [referring to] a slave who does not want to be circumcised, which implies that he is obligated to sell him; but why [must he sell him]? Let him circumcise him against his will! And similarly it is difficult, for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi holds in [chapter] HaSholeach (Gittin 39b and there): "[If one says,] 'I have despaired of my slave so-and-so,' that slave has no remedy except through a bill [of emancipation]," thus he does not hold that [statement] of Shmuel nearby, and if so, he expounds "a slave who is a man — you may circumcise him against his will"; yet later on he says: "One who buys a slave from an idolater and he did not want to be circumcised, he bears with him up to twelve months" — let him circumcise him against his will! And Rabbi Yitzchak says that it is a Rabbinic enactment, so that he will not cause his master to stumble in [matters of] forbidden and permitted [foods], since he does not accept upon himself the yoke of mitzvot; and furthermore, it is not good to obligate him in mitzvot since he has no desire to fulfill them.

Tosafot on Yevamot 48a:4:1.hebrew: המפקיר עבדו יצא לחירות ואין צריך גט שחרור - תימה, לשמואל תקשי ליה: למה ליה שטרא בעבד כנעני? יפקירנו ולימא ליה באפי בי תרי: "זיל"! דהכי דייק בפ"ק דקידושין (דף טז. ושם) גבי עבד עברי: "למה לי שטרא? לימא ליה באפי בי תרי: זיל!", ומשני: "עבד עברי גופו קנוי". ואר"י, דהכי פריך: למה לי שטרא? דאותו לשון עצמו הכתוב בשטר — "הרי את בן חורין", "הרי את לעצמך" — יאמר לו בעל פה! דס"ד דאין צריך אלא מחילה מחוב שעליו. ומסיק דגופו קנוי, ואין הלשון הכתוב בשטר מועיל בעל פה; אבל הפקר, שמסלק רשותו, מועיל אפי' בעל פה לשמואל. וא"ת: אמאי לא חשיב הפקר גבי קנינים של עבד בפ"ק דקדושין (גז"ש)? וי"ל, דלא חשיב אלא קנינים שמקנה הרב לעבד עצמו, והפקר אינו אלא סילוק בעלמא, שהרב מסלק עצמו מן העבד. ועוד יש לומר: דמילתא דאיתא בכל מילי לא קתני, כדקאמר התם לענין חליפין, "ותנא דידן מילתא דאיתא במטלטלין לא קתני":
Tosafot on Yevamot 48a:4:1.english: One who renounces ownership of his slave, [the slave] goes free and does not require a bill of emancipation - It is astonishing: according to Shmuel, there should be a difficulty — why does [a master] need a document [of emancipation] for a Canaanite slave? Let him renounce ownership of him and say to him in the presence of two [witnesses], "Go!" For thus [the Gemara] infers in the first chapter of Kiddushin (16a and there) regarding a Hebrew slave: "Why do I need a document? Let him say to him in the presence of two [witnesses]: 'Go!'" And [the Gemara] answers: "A Hebrew slave's body is owned [by his master]." And Rabbi Yitzchak says that this is what [the Gemara] is asking: Why do I need a document? Let him say to him orally the very same wording that is written in the document — "Behold, you are a free man," [or] "Behold, you are for yourself"! For it would enter your mind that nothing is needed other than a waiver of the debt that is upon him. And [the Gemara] concludes that his body is owned, and [therefore] the wording written in a document is not effective orally; however, renunciation of ownership, which removes his authority [over the slave], is effective even orally according to Shmuel. And if you ask: Why does [the Mishnah] not count renunciation of ownership among the acquisitions of a slave in the first chapter of Kiddushin (this too is there)? One can answer: That it only counts acquisitions in which the master transfers ownership to the slave himself, whereas renunciation of ownership is merely a removal [of ownership], in that the master removes himself from the slave. And furthermore, one can say: That a matter that applies to all things is not taught [by the Tanna], just as [the Gemara] says there regarding exchange (chalipin), "And our Tanna does not teach a matter that applies to movable property."
